description: Quantize a full-scale sinusoid, triangle wave or three-harmonic waveform with 1 to 16 bits. Time plots show the quantized staircase and the error, and an FFT of the error shows how oversampling and first- or second-order noise shaping change the signal-to-quantization-noise ratio in the signal band.

educational.topic: Uniform quantization, quantization noise, oversampling and noise shaping
learningObjectives: Explain why quantization is irreversible and why the error is bounded by half a step
Predict the SQNR of a full-scale sinusoid from the bit depth
Describe the quantization error in time and in frequency, and say when the white-noise model fails
Explain how oversampling and noise shaping raise the in-band SQNR without lowering the total noise

equations: white-noise model: noise power = delta^2 / 12, spread evenly from 0 to fs/2
SQNR = 6.02 b + 1.76 dB for a full-scale sinusoid
noise transfer function: 1 - z^-1 (1st order), (1 - z^-1)^2 (2nd order)
assumptions: Mid-rise uniform quantizer with levels at the midpoints of the steps
The signal band is 0 to 20 kHz and the sampling rate is OSR times 40 kHz
The measured SQNR uses a 512 x OSR point FFT of the error over 7 whole cycles of the signal
The noise shaper is an error-feedback loop whose quantizer has extra headroom levels beyond full scale
The low-pass filter is ideal (FFT bins above 20 kHz are set to zero)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict from the formula, then compare with a value measured from the samples
keyQuestions: How many decibels of SQNR does each extra bit add?
Why does oversampling a coarsely quantized sinusoid gain less than the white-noise model predicts?
Does noise shaping reduce the total quantization noise?
commonMisconceptions: Quantization error is always white noise that is unrelated to the signal
Oversampling adds resolution without any filtering
assessmentOpportunities: Predict the SQNR at 8 and 16 bits and compare with the measured values
Compare the in-band and total noise with noise shaping off, first order and second order at 16x oversampling
